questions.def: 'Had to' expresses past obligation because 'was raining' is past.
questions.question: Because it was raining, we ___ stay home.

questions.def: 'Must' expresses necessity despite the tiredness.
questions.question: Although he is tired, he ___ finish his work.

questions.def: 'Had studied' shows she studied BEFORE going to bed (past perfect).
questions.question: After she ___, she went to bed.

questions.def: 'Met' is the simple past, correct after 'since' for a past event.
questions.question: Since I ___ you, I have been happy.

questions.def: 'When' indicates the specific time of arrival for the call.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'as soon as' when referring to the future.
questions.question: I'll go home as soon as I ___ this task.

questions.def: 'Go' is the simple present, showing a habitual action.
questions.question: Before I ___ to bed, I brush my teeth.

questions.def: 'Was' matches 'was cleaning' for parallel past continuous actions.
questions.question: While I ___ cooking, she was cleaning.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'if' when referring to a future condition.
questions.question: We won't go if it ___.

questions.def: 'Gets' agrees with 'she' and is present simple for a result.
questions.question: Because she studies hard, she ___ good grades.

questions.def: 'When' indicates the time I eat dinner: when I am hungry.
questions.question: I eat dinner ___ I am hungry.

questions.def: 'Waited' is the past participle after 'have'.
questions.question: I will call you as soon as I have ___.

questions.def: 'Won't' (will not) indicates future refusal based on a condition.
questions.question: I ___ go to the party unless I finish my work.

questions.def: 'I went to bed' maintains the past tense consistent with 'was late'.
questions.question: Even though it was late, ___.

questions.def: 'Had left' indicates the action happened before 'felt sad'.
questions.question: After he ___, I felt sad.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition for helping.
questions.question: I will help you ___ you need it.

questions.def: 'I went to sleep' maintains the past tense with 'was tired'.
questions.question: Because I was tired, ___.

questions.def: 'Arrived' is simple past as the calling happened after arrival.
questions.question: I called her as soon as I ___.

questions.def: 'Was making' shows the continuous action interrupted by the phone.
questions.question: While she ___ dinner, the phone rang.

questions.def: 'He went out' maintains the past tense with 'ate'.
questions.question: After he ate, ___.

questions.def: 'Studied' is past simple because passing the exam is in the past.
questions.question: Because she ___ hard, she passed the exam.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a condition for staying home.
questions.question: I will stay home ___ it rains.

questions.def: 'You will be late' shows the consequence of not hurrying.
questions.question: Unless you hurry, ___.

questions.def: After 'although' + past, the main clause is also in the past.
questions.question: Although it was raining, she ___ to the park.

questions.def: After 'started,' we often use 'to + infinitive' to indicate an action.
questions.question: He started ___ when the movie began.

questions.def: 'After' indicates the past perfect for the first action.
questions.question: After she ___ dinner, she went out.

questions.def: 'When' shows the time relationship between arriving and calling.
questions.question: She will call ___ she arrives at the hotel.

questions.def: Past tense in both clauses because 'was' and 'helped'.
questions.question: Even though he was busy, he ___ me.

questions.def: After 'didn't', use the base form of the verb ('pass').
questions.question: Even though she had studied, she didn't passed the test.

questions.def: 'Until' with a completed time frame requires past simple.
questions.question: He ___ in London until he was ten.
